title: Korean restaurant in Fort Lee
assumptions: The company still has to be formed (an LLC) unless an entity is named. Hires staff. Builds out the space. No new exterior sign (signage: false).

items.name: Certificate of formation
items.agency: NJ Division of Revenue and Enterprise Services
items.match: certificate of formation|business formation|nj-formation|public records filing
items.quote: First, file a Certificate of formation/authorization.
items.note: Fee wording on the page is ambiguous for LLCs; not scored.

items.name: Employer Identification Number (EIN)
items.note: IRS: "You never have to pay a fee for an EIN."

items.name: Tax and employer registration (Form NJ-REG)
items.agency: NJ Division of Revenue and Enterprise Services
items.quote: Second, after filing the certificate of formation/authorization, file the tax/employer registration form (Form NJ-REG).

items.name: Retail food establishment license
items.agency: Borough of Fort Lee Health Department
items.match: (retail food|food establishment license|food license).*(fort lee)|(fort lee).*(retail food|food establishment license|food license)
items.quote: Retail Food Establishment License Fees and Application
items.note: Listed among the Health Department's applications; the fee sheet itself couldn't be read (connection reset).

items.name: Food establishment plan review
items.agency: Borough of Fort Lee Health Department
items.note: New Jersey's food code calls for plans before construction (N.J.A.C. 8:24-9.1), but Fort Lee's own procedure wasn't read.

items.name: Construction permit for the build-out
items.agency: Borough of Fort Lee Building Department
items.match: (construction permit|building permit|build-?out|tenant improvement).*(fort lee)|(fort lee).*(construction permit|building permit|build-?out|tenant improvement)
items.quote: Our Inspectors are licensed by the State of NJ and are here to make sure your construction is performed to the New Jersey Uniform Construction Code

items.name: Workers' compensation insurance
items.agency: New Jersey Department of Labor, Division of Workers' Compensation
items.note: Added in the coverage audit of 2026-10-22: bought from an insurer once there is staff.
items.quote: All corporations operating in New Jersey must maintain Workers' Compensation insurance or be approved for self-insurance

order.why: Certificate of formation first, then NJ-REG.
IRS: "form your entity through the secretary of state before you apply for an EIN."
